title: Graphical Exploration of the Horizontal Shift Parameter C
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Consider f(x) = A\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{B}(x - C)\right) + D with A = 3, B = 6, and D = 0, so f(x) = 3\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}(x - C)\right). (a) Describe what happens to the graph on [-4\pi, 4\pi] as C increases through positive values C = 0, 1, 2. (b) What happens for negative values of C? (c) What smallest positive value of C produces a graph with no net horizontal shift relative to C = 0?
finalAnswer: \text{(a) Shifts right by } C; \quad \text{(b) shifts left by } |C|; \quad \text{(c) } C = 6

steps.title: Part (a): Effect of Increasing Positive C
steps.explanation: As C increases through positive values (C = 0, 1, 2), the entire sine wave translates rigidly to the right by C units without changing its amplitude 3 or period 6.
steps.why: Replacing x with x - C in any function g(x) shifts its graph C units to the right when C > 0.

steps.title: Part (b): Effect of Negative Values of C
steps.explanation: For negative values of C, the graph translates horizontally to the left by |C| units.
steps.why: Replacing x with x + |C| shifts a graph to the left by |C| units.

steps.title: Part (c): Smallest Positive C Producing No Net Horizontal Shift
steps.explanation: Because the fundamental period of the wave is B = 6, shifting the graph horizontally by one full period C = 6 maps every peak, trough, and zero onto the next cycle, leaving the graph identical to the unshifted C = 0 curve.
steps.why: The smallest positive period of sin((pi/3)*x) is B = 2*pi/(pi/3) = 6.
